findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
6-202.16: The exit door in the facility has a visible gap with light present. Ensure a replacement seal is attached to the door to protect the establishment form the weather and entry of insects, rodents, and animals. This is a repeat from last inspection. 
6-202.16: Perimeter walls and roofs of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall effectively protect the establishment from the weather and the entry of insects, rodents, and other animals.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
4-904.11: The single service utensils are observed stored with the handles and mouth portion of the utensil intermixed. PIC was made aware of this and the utensils will be fixed and stored properly with all handles facing the same direction to prevent contamination.
4-904.11: (A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination. (B) UTENSILS not prewrapped shall be presented so only handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and/or CONSUMERS. (C) SINGLE-SERVCIE ARTICLES intended for FOOD- and lip-contact shall be furnished for CONSUMER with wrapper or APPROVED dispenser.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text: 750.120 Milk cooler was not holding proper cold holding temperatures. Bottom milk crates were 43F with probe thermometer, top crates were 47F-50F and discarded. Follow up on milk cooler 5/1/15.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.comment:
Both faucets at 3 compartment sink spray water when turned on. Repair plumbing.
750-1060 All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
Hand sink was separating from the wall. Seal sink to wall.
750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
SECOND REPEAT > Observed the milk cooler in the dry storage area to be corroded on the interior bottom. Repair cooler interior so it is smooth and easily cleanable.
750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed the interior bottom of the gym milk cooler to be soiled with an accumulation of food splash and spillage along with standing water. Clean the interior on the milk cooler.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.comment:
750.690

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment:
Squirt bottles of salad dressing were unlabeled as to their contents.  The bottles were labeled to CORRECT the violation.

750-130f Unless its identity is unmistakable, bulk food such as cooking oil, syrup, salt, sugar or flour not stored in the product container or package in which it was obtained, shall be stored in a container identifying the food by common name.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
(A) The wood shelves under the service counter and in the dry goods storage room are worn and beginning to chip.  Sand and paint the shelves.  Use a light colored glossy paint. 750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.comment:
The waste basket in the staff restroom used by kitchen employees had no cover.
750-1110d Toilet facilities shall be kept clean and in good repair and free of objectionable odors. A supply of toilet tissue shall be provided at each toilet at all times. Easily cleanable, covered receptacles shall be provided for waste materials.
Provide a covered waste basket for the restroom.,

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text: 750.120 - Pans of mashed potatoes and scrambled eggs in the 2 door cooler had internal temperatures of 43F-50F. All other products in the cooler were at 41F/below. Both products were discarded. Cold potentially hazardous foods must be held at 41F/below. Maintain foods at proper temperature. (see general comments)

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: 750.800b - The following food contact surfaces were soiled: A) can opener (debris stuck to it); B) fan blowing in kitchen toward food prep area (dust buildup); & C) container holding clean tongs (debris in the bottom of the container. Wash, rinse, and sanitize the above items and all food contact surfaces between uses/as needed to eliminate buildup of food, dust, and other debris. Container and tongs were placed in first compartment of 3 part sink to be cleaned/sanitized. Can opener was cleaned/sanitized during the inspection.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.citation_text: 750.860 - Container holding clean tongs had debris in the bottom (appeared to be mainly dust and crumbs). Cleaned and sanitized utensils an equipment shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means. Container and tongs were placed in first compartment of 3 part sink to be cleaned/sanitized.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.citation_text: 750.880 - Paper food boats in a package on the shelf below the counter had crumbs on them. Single-service articles shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in closed cartons or containers which protect them from contamination. Boats that were soiled were discarded in the trash. Kitchen manager commented paper boats were not supposed to be stored in the area where they were observed when the package hasn't been properly closed. Kitchen manager closed the bag with a twist tie to protect the remaining items from potential contamination.

findings.title: Presence of insects/rodents.  Animals prohibited
findings.citation_text: 750.1160 - Ants were observed along the walls in the gym/cafeteria by the door frame to the table storage room and by the door to the kitchen. Old cheese, a syrup packet, and an individual plastic-ware bag were observed on the floor. Effective measures must be taken to minimize the presence of pests. Cheryl McBride called the District 186 exterminator during the inspection. Area around tiles and door frames that need to be properly sealed (caulked) were pointed out to custodial and District staff. Keep floors clean, and make sure debris along walls and in corners is removed daily to eliminate potential food sources for pests. **If more time is needed to alleviate the issue, contact the inspector for an extension to the follow up.**

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text: 750.1200 & 1220 - A) Old cheese, a syrup packet, and an individual plastic-ware bag were observed on the floor. Ants were observed along the walls where the debris was located (see #35a). The custodian came in and swept the floor during the inspection. Keep floors clean, and make sure debris along walls and in corners is removed daily to eliminate potential food sources for pests. B) Ants were observed walking around/under tiles and around door frames that need to be properly sealed (caulked) by the table storage room. Other spots in the floor to wall joint of the gym/cafeteria were also pointed out to custodial and District staff. Properly seal/repair all cracks and crevices where ants were observed and throughout the gym/cafeteria.

findings.title: Outer openings protected from insects, rodent proof
findings.citation_text:
750.1170 - Threshold on gym/cafeteria doors will be replaced, metal plate will be used to cover rusted out areas on outside, & weather stripping will be replaced.

Kitchen door weather stripping will be repaired - may also change threshold.

findings.title: Outer openings protected from insects, rodent proof
findings.citation_text: 750.1170 - The outer kitchen door and the gym/cafeteria doors still have gaps in the corners (big enough for mice to fit through). One violation is being cited for the doors. The gaps in the corners of the gym/cafeteria doors especially need to be addressed. Also, gym/cafeteria doors have a least one area that is rusted out on the outside of the door (right hand side) which makes light visible on the threshold (possible entry point for insects). The rusted out area needs to be filled in with some sort of weather proof repair material(s). Openings to the outside shall be protected against the entrance of rodents and insects. Repair any and all questionable/damaged areas of the outer doors in kitchen and gym/cafeteria. (see general comments)

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text: 750.1200 - Main gas line opening in the floor behind the ovens is still not properly sealed. Steel wool has been placed in the opening. This was first cited during the February 2011, and the inspector was told the issue was addressed at the May 2011 inspection (not able to look behind ovens during May inspection). With cold holing equipment moved at this time it was possible to see the issue still needs to be addressed. All floors must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents. Have the opening properly repaired so it is sealed off to eliminate potential access by rodents and other pests.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.citation_text: 750.690 - A small hole was observed in the back corner of the freezer by the screen door. Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition. Repair the broken spot in the back of the freezer using an approved repair material (no cardboard, tape, etc.).

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: 750.800b - The can opener blade had dried food debris on it. Wash, rinse, and sanitize the can opener between uses/as needed to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of debris. When the can opener is not in use and has been used recently place it by the 3 part sink so it is clear the staff intends to properly clean/sanitize the equipment.

findings.title: Outer openings protected from insects, rodent proof
findings.citation_text: 750.1170 - (x2) A) The outer door in the kitchen had gaps underneath and in the corners where light was visible. The screen door in the kitchen also had gaps, and the lower left corner showed evidence of rodent gnawing. B) The gymnasium/cafeteria doors had gaps underneath where stripping was worn and light was visible. Openings to the outside shall be protected against the entrance of rodents and insects. Repair the doors in question so they are tight fitting/vermin proof. Make sure the corners of all the doors are sealed along with the bottom and sides. The outer door in the kitchen can not be left open as long as the screen door is not tight fitting.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text: 750.1200 - Gaps were observed in the floor to wall joint in the side room where lunch tables are stored. Junctures between walls and floors shall be coved and sealed, or shall not present an opening of more that 1/32 of an inch. Properly repair the floor to wall joint in the table storage room. Check the floor to wall joints throughout and make any needed repairs.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.citation_text: 750.1210 - A few holes were observed in the walls of the side where lunch tables are stored. All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Properly repair the walls in the table storage room. Check walls and wall junctures throughout and make any needed repairs.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 750.800e - The filters to exhaust system over ovens were dusty. Clean the filters and all non-food contact surfaces daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.citation_text: 750.860 - Clean serving spoons for the salad bar were observed in a storage container with handles and food surfaces intermixed. Cleaned and sanitized utensils and equipment shall be stored and handled in a manner which protects them from potential contamination. Store utensils all facing one direction with handles extended out so staff are not touching food surfaces when utensils are being retrieved.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text: 750.1200 - Main gas line opening in the floor behind the ovens is not properly sealed. Kitchen manager has placed steel wool in the opening but said it looked as though the material had been dislodged at one time (possibly by a mouse). A repair person was on site sealing areas in disrepair at one time but forgot to address the opening in question. All floors must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents. Have the opening properly repaired so it is sealed off to eliminate potential access by rodents and other pests.
